tasks.short: Connect business systems so teams can share reliable information.

steps.what: Agree which information teams need to share and who owns it.
Inspect interfaces, field definitions, permissions and sample records.
Resolve field meanings, ownership, validation rules and acceptable sharing.
Configure connections and transformations between the source and destination.
Test transfers and reconcile counts, values, failures and duplicate handling.
Approve activation, confirm rollback arrangements and release the connection.

tasks.design: Configure supported connectors in the {WORKFLOW} between the {ERP} and {CRM}, using an approved integration contract. A deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} checks schema changes, reconciles transfers and opens exceptions in the {HELPDESK}. The system owner approves production activation after reviewing test and rollback evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teams disagreed about field meanings, access was fragmented, and connector testing required repeated manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors handle standard transfers. AI coding can help build missing reconciliation checks, although local effort still needs measurement.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting ownership, unsupported interfaces, historical data defects and changes to business meanings.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate what a shared record means and which team must resolve a disagreement.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time configuring transfers and checking totals, and more time resolving ownership and recurring defects. They can recommend corrective work weekly; authority to change business meanings remains with data owners.

reach.task: Define acceptance limits for shared operational records.
reach.learn: Sampling, defect severity and evidence needed to release a process change.

evidence.claim: Configured connectors and deterministic reconciliation can handle stable, explicitly mapped transfers.
AI coding assistance is available for building missing integration checks; this does not establish a deployment speedup.
GDPR applies to personal-data transfers; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed use.

assumptions: The example connects the {ERP} and {CRM}; the same pattern can serve other authorised system pairs.
Supported connectors and separate test environments exist. Bespoke application development is covered by the programming task.
The integration contract can express mappings, validation, retries and duplicate handling without model interpretation.
Estimates cover one modest integration and include access and applicable consultation effort. External waiting periods can extend elapsed time.
Production activation is gated; configuration and test writes occur in an isolated environment.
unknowns: Which systems, connectors, interface limits and licences are available?
Who can approve data sharing and production activation?
Does the transfer contain employee or other personal data?
Do national rules require employee consultation for this change?
research_questions: Can existing connector configuration express the mapping without custom code?
Which failures require reconciliation rather than simple retries?
What baseline measures capture transfer accuracy and time spent resolving exceptions?
new_work: Review reconciliation exceptions and unexpected schema changes.
Maintain mappings, credentials and connector versions.
Retest duplicate handling and rollback after material changes.

tasks.short: Develop and maintain application code that meets agreed business needs.

steps.what: Clarify requested behaviour, constraints and acceptance examples with the process owner.
Inspect source repository, development tooling and relevant interface documentation.
Choose component boundaries, data handling and failure behaviour.
Write application code and tests in development tooling.

loop.input: One scoped change design, acceptance examples, permitted source files and interface definitions.
loop.output: A draft code change and tests in an isolated branch.
loop.check: Compile, run existing regression tests, check independent acceptance examples and scan dependencies and code.
loop.stop: At most three draft-and-check attempts per change; unresolved failures return to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle scaffolding, but bespoke behaviour requires interpreting requirements and existing code.

steps.what: Run automated build, regression and security checks in development tooling.
Review behaviour and maintainability, then approve merging in source repository tooling.
Approve deployment and release through deployment tooling.

tasks.design: Use the {PROJECT} to hold scoped acceptance criteria and configure source repository and development tooling in {OTHER} to supply bounded change context. Generate standard scaffolding deterministically, then use a bounded model loop for bespoke code drafts. Configured checks produce evidence, while separate review and release approvals control merging and deployment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Custom behaviour required substantial hand coding, while weak acceptance examples made generated changes difficult to verify.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance can draft scoped changes, and established build and scanning tools provide repeatable checks. Benefits depend on repository quality and reviewer effort.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous requirements, architectural consequences, missing regression coverage and failures that appear only under real workloads.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether behaviour solves the business problem and whether the code will remain understandable.
tasks.altitude: The analyst can spend more of the week testing business behaviour and delivering small improvements. They can recommend which small changes to attempt; merge and production decision rights remain explicit and separate.

reach.task: Slice requested improvements into independently releasable changes.
reach.learn: Dependency management, acceptance criteria and release sequencing.

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot provides coding assistance and review features with expected human oversight.
Aikido Security provides code, dependency and cloud scanning and proposed fixes.
Field experiments reported more completed developer tasks, but do not establish this team's expected gain.
A randomised study found experienced developers took longer with AI, supporting local measurement.

assumptions: The analyst writes modest application changes; larger engineering work is shared with developers.
Existing source repository, build and deployment tooling are represented by {OTHER}.
Build estimates cover the assistance workflow for one repository, not rebuilding an application.
The model loop has no production credentials and cannot merge or deploy.
A named reviewer can assess generated code independently of its generated tests.
Access includes checking source-code and personal-data handling under GDPR. Employee consultation under national rules applies if the workflow introduces employee monitoring.
unknowns: What regression coverage and acceptance examples already exist?
Which code and data may be supplied to model processing?
Who has merge and deployment authority?
Does existing tooling support isolated branches and reproducible checks?
Would usage measurement require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which recurring changes can be replaced entirely by templates or existing configuration?
Does assistance reduce elapsed delivery time after review and rework are included?
Which independent tests detect plausible but incorrect implementations?
new_work: Review generated drafts and reject unnecessary complexity.
Maintain acceptance examples and test fixtures.
Handle failed model attempts and newly discovered vulnerabilities.
Measure delivery time, rework and defects without unnecessary employee monitoring.

tasks.short: Translate processing needs into feasible system designs and agreed specifications.

steps.what: Interview process owners about needs, constraints and troublesome cases.
Inspect configurations, interfaces and representative processing records.
Document processes, data entities, relationships and unresolved requirements.

loop.input: Requirements notes, permitted current-state evidence and a fixed modelling schema.
loop.output: Draft requirements, process relationships and data entities with source references and open questions.
loop.check: Validate schema and references; compare technical entities with observed definitions; analyst checks business meanings.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per evidence pack; unresolved claims remain explicit open questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Schemas generate technical diagrams directly, but interview notes express implicit requirements in free text.

steps.what: Compare design options against capacity, cost, security and operational constraints.
Validate the proposed design and agree requirements and tradeoffs.
Publish the agreed specification and link requirements to delivery work.

tasks.design: Collect permitted configuration evidence from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} through scheduled read-only jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Generate technical diagrams from schemas and use a bounded extraction loop to turn notes in the {DOCS} into traceable draft requirements. After owners agree the design, deterministic templates publish the baseline in the {DOCS} and linked work in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was dispersed, diagrams drifted from actual systems, and interview notes needed careful manual interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Schema extraction and document generation are established techniques. Bounded text extraction can reduce transcription work while preserving source references.
tasks.still_hard: Unspoken needs, conflicting priorities, uncertain future loads and operational consequences that only users can explain.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the real problem behind a requested feature and make defensible tradeoffs under uncertainty.

ambition.what: Design clinics for small operations teams

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time copying evidence and maintaining specifications, leaving room for smaller teams' design questions. They gain capacity to recommend experiments; budget and design approval rights remain with the relevant owners.

reach.task: Assess whether process changes could remove the need for a system feature.
reach.learn: Process observation, benefit measurement and organisational change.

reach.task: Define recovery requirements for a proposed system design.
reach.learn: Business impact analysis, dependencies and recovery tradeoffs.

evidence.claim: Schema extraction and templates can generate technical documentation and traceability records.
SharePoint autofill columns demonstrates prompt-based document metadata extraction; its documentation warns of incorrect results.
Extracting useful requirements does not establish that a proposed architecture meets business needs.

assumptions: The example concerns an operational process using the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Process owners provide notes and representative cases; meeting recording is unnecessary.
Estimates cover one process area, a fixed modelling schema and a small set of evidence sources.
Evidence collection uses minimum necessary data under GDPR, without introducing individual employee performance analysis.
Access and consultation estimates include applicable national rules; formal consultation can add elapsed waiting time.
unknowns: Which system metadata can be exported reliably?
Are process maps and capacity baselines current?
Who can approve requirements, architecture and operational risk?
Does the evidence contain personal data or commercially sensitive material?
Which national consultation requirements apply to proposed process changes?
research_questions: Which models can be generated directly from technical definitions?
How often do extracted requirements omit exceptions or confuse preferences with obligations?
Can users validate a small prototype before committing to a full design?
new_work: Review source references and resolve extracted ambiguities.
Maintain modelling schemas and evidence connectors.
Refresh baselines when interfaces or approved requirements change.
Check whether small-team design clinics produce useful, actionable decisions.

tasks.short: Agree system principles with management and record the resulting decisions.

steps.what: Gather existing principles, design decisions and unresolved exceptions.
Prepare a brief explaining choices, consequences and questions for management.

loop.input: A fixed evidence pack, existing principles and a short briefing template.
loop.output: A draft brief with cited choices, consequences, disagreements and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require source references for factual claims; analyst checks omissions, tone and unsupported implications.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per meeting; missing evidence becomes a question for management.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief, but summarising conflicting free-text arguments requires interpretation.

steps.what: Discuss priorities, challenge assumptions and negotiate acceptable system principles.
Approve principles, exceptions and named decision owners.
Publish decisions, notify affected teams and assign follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Generate an evidence pack from approved records in the {DOCS} and unresolved work in the {PROJECT}, then use a bounded drafting loop for a reviewed discussion brief. Management negotiates and approves principles through a structured decision record. A configured flow in the {WORKFLOW} publishes approved decisions, sends internal notices through the {EMAIL} and assigns agreed actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main work was reaching agreement, while preparation and follow-up were scattered across documents and messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured decision records and configured flows can remove repeated copying. Bounded drafting can shorten briefing preparation without replacing negotiation.
tasks.still_hard: Competing incentives, budget tradeoffs, trust and management's willingness to make an explicit decision.
tasks.human_edge: Build agreement across interests and recognise when apparent consensus hides unresolved objections.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time assembling briefs and distributing decisions, with more room to prepare difficult conversations. Decision rights do not change; management remains accountable for principles and exceptions.

reach.task: Translate approved principles into project constraints and escalation points.
reach.learn: Governance, stakeholder mapping and decision escalation.

reach.task: Coordinate operational adoption of an agreed system principle.
reach.learn: Service ownership, practical rollout constraints and communication needs.

evidence.claim: Structured decision records can drive deterministic publication, internal notifications and action assignment.
TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for review, demonstrating reviewed drafting of internal explanatory text.
Negotiating system principles requires accountable human choices; document automation does not establish agreement.

assumptions: Management already meets to resolve system principles and exceptions.
Approved decisions can be captured in structured fields before publication.
Notifications use the approved decision text and agreed recipients.
Estimates cover one decision template, one approval route and existing internal systems.

Access review covers GDPR and confidentiality. Employee consultation under national rules is included where a proposed principle affects employees; wider implementation consultation is outside this small briefing workflow.
unknowns: Who has authority to approve principles and exceptions?
Where are authoritative decisions currently stored?
Which decisions can be distributed broadly?
Do proposed principles affect employee monitoring, work organisation or other consultation rights?
research_questions: What information does management repeatedly lack when a decision is deferred?
Can existing approval and notification configuration cover the entire publication step?
Does a shorter reviewed brief improve decision clarity without omitting dissent?
new_work: Review briefing drafts for missing objections and unsupported implications.
Maintain decision templates, approval routes and distribution groups.
Resolve overdue actions and outdated principles.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward clarifying needs, testing business behaviour and negotiating system tradeoffs. Routine collection, configuration and publication shrink; business, merge and production approvals remain with named human owners.
reach: Partner with management analysts to remove unnecessary process steps before specifying technology.
Help information technology project managers turn designs into small, verifiable releases.
Work with business continuity planners and quality control systems managers on recovery and acceptance requirements.
skills_to_grow: Data contracts, interface design and deterministic reconciliation.
Independent acceptance testing and secure code review.
Evidence-based requirements modelling and source traceability.
Facilitation, operational tradeoffs and decision documentation.
GDPR data minimisation, applicable EU AI Act duties and consultation under national rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a repeatable operations improvement service: diagnose a small process problem, test a design, deliver a scoped change and measure its effect. Reuse templates, connectors and checks across teams while keeping local access, ownership and approval explicit.
